title: Friuli-Venezia Giulia's Fuel Prices Edge Above the National Average
dek: Self-service Benzina and Gasolio in Italy's northeastern region both run ahead of the national mean, with diesel pushing toward €2.21 a litre.
body: As of September 3, 2026, drivers in Friuli-Venezia Giulia paid an average of €2.0655 per litre for self-service Benzina and €2.2062 for self-service Gasolio. Both figures sit above Italy's national self-service averages of €2.0513 and €2.1766 respectively — Benzina running about 1.4 cents higher and Gasolio nearly 3 cents higher than the rest of the country.

The regional trend has been gently upward: self-service Benzina climbed from €2.0479 to €2.0655 over the past several tracked days, while Gasolio dipped briefly before rising again to €2.2062. Of the 521 fuel stations registered in the region, 467 reported prices on the latest collection day — a slight dip from 468 the time before, but still a healthy slice of the local network staying active and visible.

Tracking this kind of granular, region-by-region detail every single day — accurate to the cent, refreshed automatically — would be a nightmare to maintain by hand in a spreadsheet. Fuel Dashboard does it without a single manual update: built with Claude Code, it pulls Italy's official MIMIT price data, crunches the numbers, and rebuilds itself daily, region by region, so stories like Friuli-Venezia Giulia's small diesel uptick don't get lost in a national average.
